result.summary: Configure Guix to build Linux x86_64 and aarch64 non-GUI release binaries (bitcoind and CLI tools) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44. Apply patches to glibc to eliminate non-deterministic /gnu/store paths and disable NSS module runtime dlopening. Adjust Guix symbol-check and security-check verification scripts to support and validate static ELF binaries.
result.problem: Linux release binaries dynamically link against glibc and the system dynamic linker, preventing them from running on non-glibc distributions like Alpine Linux or on systems with glibc versions older than the build environment. Dynamic linking also complicates security mitigations such as aarch64 pointer authentication (#19075).
evidence: PR description: shows `file bitcoind` reporting `ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable ... static-pie linked` and `ldd` reporting `statically linked` across multiple distributions including Alpine, CentOS, Debian, and NixOS.

doc/release-notes-25573.md: notes release binaries for x86_64 and aarch64 Linux 'can now be run on non-glibc based systems, as well as on systems than ship with older glibcs' but warns that 'name resolution through dynamic nss modules is not possible' (e.g., mDNS, LDAP, SSSD).
result.scope_notes: Touches Guix build scripts, package definitions, glibc source patches (to remove store paths and dlopen behavior), and post-build ELF validation scripts.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased onto recent build system changes with no major structural alterations.
result.card: Configures Guix to build official Linux x86_64 and aarch64 release binaries (excluding bitcoin-qt) as static position-independent executables (-static-pie) using glibc 2.44. This eliminates dynamic linker dependencies, allowing bitcoind and utilities to run on musl-based distributions like Alpine Linux and on older Linux installations, while enabling aarch64 pointer authentication (#19075). Statically compiling glibc means dynamic NSS modules (such as mDNS, LDAP, or SSSD) will no longer function for name resolution. Post-build symbol and security check scripts are updated to validate static ELF binaries.

risk.why: Alters the toolchain and linking method for official Linux release binaries; a bug could break host DNS resolution or make binaries unexecutable on Linux systems.
